context.objective: Document how we carry out Carried Interest Waterfall & Clawback, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: To begin with, we confirm the trigger, purpose, model, and terms. That is done by: Preparer; advisers resolve gaps. Before starting we need trigger, current governing documents, approved model. What we do: identify the structure and calculation layer; record every applicable term and definition; confirm the version-controlled model and as-of date Output and record to keep: Locked calculation instructions.
What event prompts the preparer to begin confirming the trigger, governing documents, and approved model?

Next, we collect and reconcile cumulative inputs. That is done by: Preparer. Before starting we need accounting, transaction, valuation, prior-model data. What we do: collect cumulative inputs; match opening balances, prior carried interest, holdback, and clawback to the GL and prior approved model Output and record to keep: Reconciled input package.
When the opening balances, prior carried interest, holdback, or clawback don’t match the GL or prior approved model, what happens before the input package is considered reconciled?
I don't know, I only joined three weeks ago and have not done that part yet.
What event normally prompts the preparer to start this work?
What result is the waterfall and clawback work intended to produce?
I'm not sure. Preparer would be the person to ask.
Which entities or clients does this waterfall and clawback work cover?
I don't know how that works.
What event usually prompts the preparer to begin this work?
Who uses the reconciled input package next?
I can't say, I have not seen that happen yet.
What guides the preparer in deciding which terms and definitions apply to the calculation?
